recipes.name: Earthquake Cookies
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) package devil's food cake mix

steps.text: Mix cake mix, eggs, shortening, and water in a medium-sized bowl; mix with a spoon. Chill for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Shape dough into balls and roll in powdered sugar. Place on cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until browned, 8 to 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Earthquake Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These earthquake cookies are so easy to make, you’ll probably crumble! You can use any flavor of cake mix you like, the possibilities are endless.

review.reviewBody: I have to give these a 5 for ease of prep, versatility of recipe, few ingredients, presentation, and taste! I used a D.H. devil's food mix, and perhaps it was that particular mix, but it tasted just like I made these with Hershey cocoa powder. There was not one hint of cake mix taste that sometimes can occur with yellow and white mixes. They present so well with the cracked tops. The dough is stiff so thanks for the headsup on not mixing with a mixer. I just creamed my shortening and beat in eggs and water with electric mixer then added mix by hand. The dough is stiff enough that it is very easy to work with especially if using a cookie scoop; just scoop them into the powdered sugar and roll them around; no messy fingers. I didn't even bother to chill the dough; if pressed for time I don't think it needs to be. The cracked top looks just like a blacktop highway that has crumbled from an earthquake. Perhaps that is why they are called this? I'd not hesitate to put these on a christmas cookie tray they are just that attractive and good.

I have made these for years. My favorite cake mix is double fudge. Lemon is second. If you like more zing with lemon like I do, add 1-2 Tb. of lemon zest and add ascorbic acid to the powdered sugar. Start with just a touch, 1/8 t. Sift well. Totally awesome. If you like an awesome dessert, turn this into a pizza-roll out or pat on a pizza pan ( I prefere stone)to within 1inch of edge. Use the Dble. fudge. Bake for 15 minutes no more. Cream 1-2 8oz pkgs of cream cheese with 2 T of butter, 1/2 c Coco Lopez. Add sifted powdered sugar to a spreadable consistancy. Spread on cooled pizza. Top with coconut and ch. pecans, walnuts or nut of your choice. If you don't want a crisp edge, carefully cut off about 1/2 inch all around and crumble on top. Enjoy. My friends love this one. If you like Mounds candy bars this is for you

Delicious and packed with flavor!! I used a Spice cake mix (DH) and added 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract. Didn’t chill the dough and rolled immediately in powdered sugar. A huge hit! Easy to make!!

Delicious and packed with flavor!! I used a Spice cake mix (DH) and added 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon and 1/2 teaspoon vanilla extract. Didn’t chill the dough and rolled immediately in powdered sugar. A huge hit! Easy to make!!

I found that it was difficult to mix with a spoon because the shortening didn't get incorporated well. So next time I used pastry cutter to mix the shortening and cake mix then added eggs and water. much easier. Oh and I did add lemon zest to the lemon cake batch. yum.

I made the cookies with little variation. I used a Pampered Chef large scoop (ping pong ball size) and this yielded about 2 dozen cookies. I did stick the dough in the freezer for 1/2 hour after chilling the dough the required hour, and couldn’t really tell a difference from the original dough consistency. I baked them for 12 minutes. Allow them to cool completely once baked, as they are on the soft side. If you like the sweet chocolate taste of brownies as I do, chocolate chips are in order. If you like a not-so-sweet chocolate cookie, you’ll probably like these. I’ll make them again as a quick and easy treat that looks pretty.

I missed the part where it said to chill for 1 hour, would've made it a lot easier to scoop but it did work and came out beautifully! And I used 1/3c of applesauce instead of shortening. Used spice cake mix and cinnamon chips, and lemon cake mix and a little lemon extract for extra flavor, Next will be chocolate fudge cake and peanut butter chips!

This is the only way I make cookies now. So easy and simple. My family loves it. You can make a variety of flavors just by changing the flavor of the cake mix or adding extract. I have added nuts, chocolate chips, coconut, and even raisins the recipe and it always turns out amazing. I made 5 different kinds of cookies just using this recipe for a holiday party with my in-laws and now it is my signature dish.

I just made Lemon Poppyseed Earthquake cookies. Really nice and light. I used a lemon cake mix, 2 eggs, 1/3 C of melted butter, 1 T of lemon juice and 1/8 C of poppy seeds. Again I scooped the 1 1/2" balls right into the icing sugar and rolled them. I got 32. This time I had to chill them for awhile. I am famous for my Lemon Poppyseed Cake, so I thought... why not?
My granddaughter and I made this together and it was very easy! Although, she accidentally put in the powdered sugar with the mix! However, it added more flavor and less crispness to the cookie.

These were great! I made mine with butter pecan cake mix ( my favorite!) and they were delicious...a great way to make/serve 'cake'. I topped mine with a dollop of buttercream icing and a sugared pecan to dress them up and make them more of a dessert. I do suggest that you watch them very closely while baking! For me, 9min was the magic time. At 8min they were a little under done and flattened out as they cooled and at 10min the bottoms burnt, so I scraped of the bottom and they still tasted fine. Also, the recipe didn't say to grease the pan and my first batch stuck to the bottom, so I suggest you lightly spray your sheet with baking spray.
Made these for a bake sale. Eye catching and good flavor with 1 cup of chocolate chips added. I did refrig for 1 hour and I think that helps develop the flavor. Made 34 with Med cookie scoop.

These have turned out beautiful. Someone suggested I try to make these. This recipe is about the easiest ever! I haven't yet heard from my renter if they are exactly what he expected. I only made one change to it. Instead of the half a cup of shortening I used 1/3 cup of coconut oil.
It is great. Used some MMs for color., inside and out. Can hardly wait to make with orange zest or craisens
Too crunchy for my taste. However, they are good-looking cookies. oo crunchy for my taste. They looked good.
Mmmmmmmm!

Super easy recipe and minimal ingredients. Going to try with lemon cake mix as another suggested, next time. These were good, but not a lot of flavor. My husband and kids loved them. Baked for 11 min, at 10 min the centers were still too soft.
I used to make Chocolate Crinkles, when in a hurry I use this receipe. This receipe with the cake mix is just as delish as the Chocate Crinkles and takes less time.
I love this recipe

I've made these cookies a half dozen times, and they're a big hit. They are nice and chewy; just be sure not to overbake. I tried it using yellow cake mix one time, but the devil's food is much better. I'll definitely use it again, and again, and again!
